title: All the key moments from the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix
excerpt:
Kimi Antonelli’s stellar sophomore campaign had left little doubt that he would win his maiden Drivers’ Championship, but he did so in style with a podium finish at the eventful Mexico City Grand Prix.

While it was a rollercoaster of a weekend for many, with Max Verstappen shaking off a grid penalty to keep Lewis Hamilton at bay and clinch victory as Ferrari faced further internal turmoil, Antonelli’s title triumph was one for the history books in more ways than one.

Here are all the key moments from the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix…

Antonelli becomes F1’s youngest champion

It always seemed likely that Antonelli would achieve his childhood dream of becoming a Formula 1 World Champion in Mexico City, with the Mercedes driver only needing ninth place, regardless of where main rivals George Russell and Hamilton finished.

Starting fourth for Sunday's 71-lap race, the 20-year-old Italian stayed out of trouble through the opening phase and circulated behind the Ferraris of Charles Leclerc and Hamilton, as well as eventual race winner Verstappen.

While the trio made their pit stops, Mercedes kept Antonelli out in the hopes of a Safety Car which eventually came – but one lap after Antonelli had already stopped.

With the Safety Car upgraded to a red flag due to barrier repairs, Antonelli once again had to face the gauntlet of a standing start from P4, which he accomplished without issue and even gained a position shortly after at the expense of Leclerc with a confident overtake into Turn 1.

Thereafter, Antonelli shadowed Verstappen and Hamilton until the chequered flag, becoming the youngest driver in history to win the F1 title and the first Italian champion since Alberto Ascari in 1953 on an historic weekend.

"Without them, I wouldn’t be here – without Mercedes, without my family," said Antonelli. "So I’m very grateful for this moment, and it’s one that will live forever. I’m speechless. I’m trying to process what has just happened.

“It’s been an incredible season, and to share this podium with Max and Lewis is truly incredible."

Why Antonelli's title win is an explosive shot in the arm for F1

Ferraris come together again on the opening lap

Although Antonelli took centre stage in Mexico after his title success, the other main talking point in the paddock was how Ferrari had seemingly thrown away a chance of victory.

Hamilton had claimed his maiden Grand Prix pole for the Scuderia and initially held his lead on the long run down to Turn 1, only for team mate Leclerc to challenge around the outside.

Having gone side-by-side, the pair went off the track at Turn 4, with Leclerc cutting the grass to take the lead, while Hamilton slipped behind Verstappen.

With Leclerc handed a five-second penalty for the incident, it meant that the Monegasque driver lost the lead and dropped behind Verstappen as both pitted at the same time.

Hamilton also jumped Leclerc at the standing restart and hounded Verstappen until the chequered flag, but the seven-time World Champion was left unimpressed by his team mate's tactics, as Leclerc accepted he deserved a penalty.

Team Principal Fred Vasseur was also left unimpressed, telling Canal+: "I'm having trouble swallowing it. It's a lack of respect for all the people who work. Wasting a victory is hard. It's stuck in my throat. They're not racing for themselves. We're going to clear all this up."

Verstappen comes out on top in a hectic race

In a hectic race with multiple storylines, it was Red Bull’s Verstappen who came out on top to win his sixth Mexico City Grand Prix.

The Dutch driver started P5 on the grid but had a great start, before taking advantage of the scrap between the two Ferraris to jump ahead of Hamilton and cause a headache by being in the way of that potential place swap.

He overtook Leclerc for the lead of the race in the pit stop where the Monegasque served his five-second time penalty, and then survived a standing restart following the red flag caused by the Cadillac of Valtteri Bottas suffering a suspension failure and crashing into the barriers.

He continued to hold off Hamilton after a late Safety Car restart, caused by a collision between Arvid Lindblad and Oscar Piastri, to cross the finish line just 0.7s ahead.

Verstappen has now won three of the last four Grands Prix, bringing home 149 points. That has shot him up to second in the Drivers’ Championship, two points ahead of Hamilton.

Verstappen on the move that earned him 'fantastic' Mexico win

Another challenging race for Russell as Mercedes ‘let him down’

It was another challenging race for Russell who started the Mexico City Grand Prix in P2 but, after a poor start, he crossed the line in sixth – whilst watching his Mercedes team mate celebrate clinching the title.

The Briton initially challenged Hamilton on the run down to the first corner but seemed to suffer with energy deployment issues, which saw him drop four places.

His pain was compounded after tapping Isack Hadjar at Turn 6, sending the Red Bull driver into a spin… that collision saw him handed a 10-second penalty by the stewards.

Russell crossed the line in P6 but that result, and the higher placing of Verstappen and Hamilton, has seen him drop to fourth in the standings.

Speaking after the race, Mercedes boss Toto Wolff said the team had let Russell down with the technical issue he suffered at the start. “I believe he was racing for the victory here and then came in this lack of energy and ruined his race," he told Sky Sports F1.

Wolff went on to acknowledge that seeing Antonelli take the title was also a difficult moment for Russell: “We have two drivers, we don’t have one. The car just didn’t work for him this year. And then misfortune like today, we just have to sort it out for him.”

Hirakawa scores on his Grand Prix debut for Haas

Ryo Hirakawa came to Mexico City expecting to compete in FP1 for Haas, and instead found himself making his Grand Prix debut. Having performed credibly in the first session, he returned to the sidelines for FP2, only to find himself promoted to a race seat after the team replaced Esteban Ocon following that second practice session.

The Japanese racer did well in Qualifying, winding up 19th but with the caveat that he picked up traffic on his final flying lap. In the Grand Prix he kept his starts clean, which could not be said for everyone. With so many incidents, Hirakawa kept a cool head and chose his moments well to pull off some overtakes despite the tricky track conditions.

He described the day as a “dream”, but even he could not have predicted what would happen next, when a raft of post-race penalties lifted him from P13 to 10th, meaning he scored on debut.

Who is F1’s latest debutant Ryo Hirakawa?

“I was trying to learn from what others were doing, and maybe the first stint was tough, but I learned a lot,” he divulged. “After the Safety Car, with the soft compound, I had more confidence and, after the last one, I had much more confidence and passed two cars, so I’m happy to finish like that.”

But emotions were not so positive on the other side of the garage, with Ollie Bearman forced into retirement with car damage. He was battling on the fringes of the points and looking competitive when he was hit from behind by Nico Hulkenberg, who was penalised for the incident.

Unfortunately, the damage was too severe for Bearman to continue, but at least Haas have the consolation of that one point to take away from Mexico City.

title: What the teams said – Race day in Mexico City
excerpt:
Mercedes

Kimi Antonelli’s race will be remembered as the one that sealed him his maiden World Championship title, the Italian finishing on the rostrum as he took the crown with four rounds to go. The Italian only needed to finish ninth but did much better than that to come home third. His race was relatively straight forward, he kept out of trouble, picked off Leclerc at the restart thanks to his rival having a flat-spot, and then kept the rest clean. The emotion came out after the chequered flag, Antonelli crying into his helmet as what he had achieved sunk in.

As for George Russell, he had a bad start from the front row and dropped back before Turn 1, before making contact with Hadjar. That earned him a 10-second time penalty and sent him back into a fight with the McLaren duo. He wound up coming home sixth, but made sure to congratulate his team mate and championship rival at the end of the race.

Kimi Antonelli, 3rd

"It’s difficult to put into words what I’m feeling right now. I’m still trying to process it all, but to be able to say that I am world champion is just incredible. This is a moment that I will remember for the rest of my life. We’ve had an amazing season and I’m so proud of what we have achieved together. From very early on, we had a strong car and were able to be consistent, and that gave us the belief that we could fight for the championship.

"I wouldn’t be here without this team and without all the people and partners who have supported me throughout my career. Mercedes has believed in me for so many years and given me this incredible opportunity, so to repay that trust by winning the World Championship together means so much. I also have to thank my family, my friends and everyone who has been there for me along the way.

"I definitely felt more tension coming into this weekend, knowing what was possible, so to get it done today is a huge relief and an amazing feeling. Finishing on the podium made it even more special and sharing it with Max (Verstappen) and Lewis (Hamilton) was really cool. We still have races to go and we want to finish the season strongly by clinching the Constructors’ Championship, but tonight we’re definitely going to enjoy this moment together as a team."

George Russell, 6th

"Firstly, congratulations to Kimi on a thoroughly deserved championship. He has done a fantastic job this season and can be incredibly proud of what he has achieved.

"Unfortunately, it was a very disappointing race on my side. I made a good start and was in a strong position, but then we suffered an issue which caused me to not have full deployment down the straight. That cost us a lot of positions and ultimately took us out of contention for a strong result. It’s frustrating to have the race compromised by something outside of my control but that is racing.

"We will reset after this weekend and look to come back stronger in Brazil. We still have a Constructors’ Championship to win and my full focus is on helping the team achieve that."

Toto Wolff, Head of Mercedes-Benz Motorsport

"What Kimi has achieved today is extraordinary. To become Formula 1 World Champion at 20 years old, and to do it in only his second season, is a remarkable achievement. But what makes me most proud is not the record or the statistics, it is the journey he has been on to get here.

"There were difficult moments last year. There were people who questioned whether he was ready for Formula One and whether he deserved to be in a Mercedes. We always believed in his talent and knew those difficult experiences would make him stronger. To see the way he has responded this season, the confidence he has built and the level at which he is now performing is incredibly satisfying. We saw that maturity again today. He managed the first stint extremely well, stayed patient when the red flag took away the advantage he had created, and then made the move when he needed to after the restart. To deliver that performance with a World Championship on the line says a lot about him.

"We also have to acknowledge George. Today was another race where we didn’t give him the platform to show what he could do. The deployment issue at the start immediately compromised his afternoon and, although the incident and penalty made his race more difficult, he kept fighting and brought the car home in P6. There have been too many occasions this season where we have let George down, and he has deserved more from us. His contribution to what we have achieved this year has been immense, and we shouldn’t lose sight of that today.

"This is a tremendous moment for everyone at Brackley and Brixworth, and all those associated with the team. Championships are never won by one individual. There are so many people who have contributed, both here at the track and back at the factories, and they should all feel incredibly proud tonight. Thank you to Mercedes-AMG for their continued support, our Title and Technical Partner PETRONAS and so many more. We all believed in Kimi from a very young age and today he is a Formula One World Champion. That is a very special moment for all of us."

Andrew Shovlin, Trackside Engineering Director

"Congratulations to Kimi on his first World Championship. It was quite an eventful race, but he did a really good job managing the Soft tyre in the first stint and was able to run it beyond 40 laps. That gave us some useful options for the end of the race, although the red flag effectively reset things and removed the tyre advantage we had created. He restarted P4 but made a very good move on Leclerc to get back into the podium positions and drove a very controlled race from there to take P3 and the title.

"He has driven superbly across the season and the way he handled the race today, with everything that was at stake, was another demonstration of the progress he has made. It’s an incredible achievement for him and he should be rightly proud of himself.

"George had a difficult afternoon through no fault of his own. The deployment issue on the run to Turn 1 cost him several positions and put him on the back foot from the very start. From there, he was having to recover in traffic and the contact with Hadjar and subsequent penalty made that task harder. He kept his head down, showed good pace and fought back to P6. It’s frustrating because we didn’t give him the start to the race that he needed and that is on us as team.

"We have plenty to focus on as we head to Brazil We want to add the Constructors’ Championship to the Drivers’ title, and we know we still must deliver the performances to do that. We’ll enjoy today, then turn our attention very quickly to the next race."

title: 'Unbelievable' – The F1 grid praise new champion Antonelli
excerpt:
The Mexico City Grand Prix saw Kimi Antonelli finish third, which was more than enough for the Italian to seal the 2026 Drivers' World Championship.

Significantly he had the opportunity to share the podium with race winner Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton, two of the all-time greats, creating a photo opportunity for the ages.

Of course the top step rather than P3 would have been the ideal scenario, but joining those legends as his celebrations got underway was something special for the youngster.

One of the remarkable aspects of Antonelli's progress towards the title is that he has generated such huge respect from colleagues and rivals on the grid, even those whose own win records he can currently only aspire to.

Verstappen and Hamilton know what it takes to put together a championship-winning season, and both recognise Antonelli’s special talent.

“I think to achieve this in your second year in F1 is always very impressive,” Verstappen said. “Because, of course, at his age as well, to be so solid, not make big mistakes, and of course, also beat your experienced team mate, he's just driven incredible.

“And I'm very proud of him, how he has handled himself this whole season. It's not always easy to deliver every single weekend, but he has done that, and he's the deserved champion this year.”

Hamilton added: “I mean, it was beautiful to be up there with these two and to be up there with Kimi for his first World Championship. I think it was a very special moment, one of the most special moments that I remember having here.”

Lando Norris, the man Antonelli follows as World Champion, was equally supportive – and after the Grand Prix he was keen to ensure that the Italian’s achievement is properly acknowledged.

“Unbelievable,” said the McLaren driver. “I think what he's done is he's blown everyone away. I hope everyone gives him enough credit for what he's achieved this year, because he's made everyone else look silly, he's driven that well, and he's been able to click with his car. He's worked hard to understand how to drive this car, and he's exploited it better than anyone else. So he deserves every single bit of success.

“He's had an unbelievable year, and it's even more impressive that it's only his second season in F1. He's 20 years old, it's incredible. So I'm very happy for him, very, very happy for him. And I'm very happy to see my number one go over to him, because he deserves it. So in a way, happy to see it go.”

Norris’ team mate Oscar Piastri understands the pressures involved in chasing the World Championship title, although as he noted in the end it wasn’t as close a battle as the one he was involved with in 2025.

“He's done an incredible job I think,” said the Australian. “In his second season in F1 to accomplish what he's accomplished this year is very, very impressive. And clearly Mercedes have done a good job around him, giving him the car to deliver, supporting him, and he's done the business as well, so a very impressive season.”

Some of the drivers who have been around for a while and are still searching for that elusive title-winning recipe could be forgiven for being a little envious about success coming so soon, but they all recognise what the Italian has acheived.

“I'm obviously very happy for him,” said Charles Leclerc. “I consider myself young, but when I look at him, he's even younger. And to see his parents underneath the podium being so emotional is a beautiful image. So I'm very, very happy for him.

“I was trying to wait for him after the chequered flag, but I guess he was going very slow to celebrate as he should, and I'll go and see him later. But it's fully deserved. I mean, he didn't put a step wrong since the beginning of the end.”

“I think completely deserved, and honestly, he's done a really, really good year,” said Carlos Sainz, a driver with more than a decade in the sport behind him. “He's known how to maximise his chance of becoming World Champion [in] his second year in F1.

"A lot of us would have wished to have such a competitive car in our first years in F1, and he did exactly that. He was given the opportunity to win a championship, and the year that it's given to him, he maximised everything.

"He did a perfect first half of the year, dominated, and then controlled the second part of the year, which is what a World Champion has to do, and I think he did it really, really well.”

Antonelli shares touching reaction to ‘incredible’ title victory

Sainz’s team mate Alex Albon is another experienced driver who admires what Antonelli has done this season.

“It's really impressive,” said the Williams driver. “I think also his mentality, at least from the outside he looked very relaxed. I heard some comments in qualifying that he was a bit tense.

"If anything, his race pace has been really impressive – so I think what's kind of separated him from the rest of the grid this year is his race pace, and of course, most probably partly car as well. But it's been really impressive to see the step he's made from last year.”

Those a little closer in age to Antonelli are just as pleased to see him win and fly the flag for the younger generation.

"Can't get any better than World Champion between the two best champions in the last era of F1,” said Franco Colapinto of the Mexico City podium.

“He deserves it. He needs to enjoy it. I think it's the dream of all of us, what he had this year. The speed, we all knew that he had it, but I think the consistency that he showed this year, race after race, being on the podium and scoring the points and not making mistakes – it's been extremely impressive to have that weight in your shoulders of being P1 in the championship for so long from the start to the end.”

For Gabriel Bortoleto, Antonelli’s success is a source of inspiration.

“We are very close on age,” said the Brazilian. “He's a bit younger than I am. I've fought for championships in F2 and F3, and I know how tense you are when you are fighting. But imagine fighting for a F1 championship against, I don't know, Russell, Max, Lewis, all these World Champions [with] so much experience – and the guy didn't break. He was always there, consistent, boom, on top.

“So an impressive job from him. And again, I hope to be fighting for titles with him in the future, because that would be a beautiful story, a guy I know since I'm like 10 years old, 11 years old, to F1, and now he's World Champion – and I'm trying to reach that game.”

title: ‘People were doubters’ – Wolff on Antonelli’s ‘incredible’ journey
excerpt:
Toto Wolff has reflected on Kimi Antonelli's journey with Mercedes after the Italian claimed his maiden Formula 1 title at the Mexico City Grand Prix.

Antonelli became the youngest World Champion in just his second season of F1 after finishing third in Sunday's race, after a season which has included nine Grand Prix wins.

It signifies a remarkable turnaround from his debut campaign, where the Italian failed to score in 10 races as Mercedes faced calls to replace him, having promoted him after just three seasons in junior single-seaters.

Speaking to Sky Sports F1 after Antonelli's title win at the age of just 20, Team Principal Wolff admitted "it was always a calculated risk, not a real risk" to promote the-then teenager into F1, and that the team always supported him even through the difficult moments.

"It's incredible, we have to pinch ourselves because it seems like yesterday he was 11 years old in the garage in junior karting. And it goes so fast," he said.

"He wins the junior formula, then a difficult year in F2 and that's already where people started to doubt. Then when Lewis [Hamilton] told me 'I'm going to Ferrari', it was my immediate reaction that we've got to put him in the car. But people were doubters.

"I was thinking before, we had two sponsors leaving us because of that, because who is this kid? There were others who stayed with us until today, some are here that reap the full reward and then the difficult year.

"People said he shouldn't even be in F1, he should be at a smaller team, 10 races and no points, the tears in Spa, and then this. I'm just so proud for the team, all of them continued to trust him and he delivered."

As well as delivering on track, Wolff also praised Antonelli in how he handles things behind the scenes, whether it is speaking with sponsors and partners, or becoming integrated in the team.

The Austrian pointed out that Antonelli's personality had won over many in the team.

"He obviously has a very winning way in the team. We're dealing with very stiff, unemotional English people," Wolff told Sky Sports F1.

"So then comes this Italian boy that starts to hug everyone in the garage and you can see how it changed the environment and now all the Brits are hugging each other, which is weird to see.

"He's a kid. He's 20 years old. You see him driving, the maturity, the interaction with the partners but then for his birthday he goes to the waterpark, and that is so great to see. I was like, 'where's Kimi I need to speak with him?' Kimi's at the waterpark with his friends. We love that."

title: 'Serious talks’ – Hamilton on costly Leclerc battle
excerpt:
Lewis Hamilton believes Ferrari "easily had a car to have P1 and P2" during the Mexico City Grand Prix, as an opening lap battle with team mate Charles Leclerc potentially cost the team victory.

The seven-time World Champion claimed his maiden Grand Prix pole position for the Scuderia ahead of Sunday's 71-lap race at the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez, showing strong pace before he held his advantage on the long run to Turn 1.

But Leclerc moved to the outside in the braking zone, with the pair running side-by-side through the opening sequence of corners as Hamilton just stayed ahead.

The Briton defended again into Turn 4 as both he and Leclerc went deep into the corner and off the track, but whereas Hamilton made an attempt to rejoin the circuit as soon as possible, Leclerc headed across the grass to take the lead.

Hamilton's loss of momentum meant he lost another position to eventual race winner Max Verstappen, with Leclerc only handed a five-second penalty for the incident, the stewards not handing out a harsher punishment as Hamilton had also gone off track.

Leclerc lost the lead to Verstappen after serving his penalty during a pit stop, with Hamilton jumping ahead of his team mate after a mid-race restart following a red flag.

Despite challenging Verstappen until the end and finishing second, Hamilton was visibly frustrated by his team mate's actions, claiming Ferrari "easily had a car to have P1 and P2 today".

"I don't really have anything to say about the scenario with Charles. I think you can see what happened and the reason we lost the win," said Hamilton.

"In the drivers’ briefing, we discussed that as soon as you go off at Turn 1, you have to give the position back, or else… Last year I got a 10-second penalty for that same move that he did.

"Ultimately, it was that that lost us the win today. And I, yeah, I think we have to have some serious talks behind the scenes for sure."

This is not the first time Leclerc and Hamilton have gone wheel-to-wheel this season, the pair having had a frenetic battle in China, while Leclerc apologised for pushing Hamilton off at the start of the Italian GP.

Hamilton admitted that a "serious conversation" would be needed, and that any internal fighting would only hold the team back.

"I think the core thing to remember, which maybe comes with age, is that every decision you make in the car impacts all the people that work in the background for the whole team," said Hamilton.

"So, working as a team is a part of our job and a part of our contract. We have to work as a team, which we could have easily done today. So, it's a shame to see us lose this, as we did. That will just continue unless action is taken, if a real deep, serious conversation is had.

"So, it shouldn't happen moving forward. Of course, I've had close battles with team mates in the past, and you can't always get it right, but nine times out of ten we should be able to.

"So, I think we'll take it offline and we'll have some good conversations, hopefully. For sure, it won't be easy, but it must be done."

title: Alpine duo stripped of Mexico City GP points after penalties
excerpt:
Franco Colapinto and Pierre Gasly have lost their respective P8 and P10 finishes at the Mexico City Grand Prix, with the Alpine pair penalised after the race for separate yellow flag infringements.

The Frenchman had outqualified his team mate at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez, but it was Colapinto who enjoyed the better start and improved from P11 to P7 over the opening laps.

Although they managed the 71-lap affair well to secure a hard-fought double points finish for Alpine, they were later summoned to the stewards for failing to slow under yellow flags – Colapinto doing so in a single yellow sector, and Gasly in a double.

Their subsequent penalties – 10 seconds for the Argentine driver and a stop-and-go for Gasly – have dropped them down the final classification and promoted Red Bull's Isack Hadjar and Haas newcomer Ryo Hirakawa to P9 and P10.

The stewards’ decision document on Colapinto, which added that he would also receive a penalty point, read: “The Stewards heard from the driver of Car 43 (Colapinto), team representative and reviewed positioning/marshalling system data, video, timing, telemetry, team radio and in-car video evidence.

“The driver and team presented telemetry and photographic evidence claiming it demonstrated that the driver had complied with the regulations which state that the driver must reduce speed and be prepared to change direction.

“A detailed examination of the telemetry and on board camera failed to satisfy the Stewards that the driver had sufficiently reduced speed through that single yellow sector.

“In relation to the previous double yellow flag sector the Stewards determined that there was sufficient doubt that the driver had sufficient warning in order to comply with the requirements, so did not determine that there was any breach in relation to that sector.”

Meanwhile, Gasly’s lack of speed reduction was determined to be a more serious error, earning him two penalty points.

The document related to him explained: “The Stewards heard from the driver of Car 10 (Gasly), team representative and reviewed positioning/marshalling system data, video, timing, telemetry and in-car video evidence.

“The driver and team representative claimed that the driver had made a significant reduction in speed in the double yellow flag sector however a detailed examination of the telemetry and that of other cars passing through that sector, led the Stewards to conclude that the small reduction noted was not sufficient to satisfy the requirements of the regulations.”

Following Oscar Piastri’s penalty for causing a collision, the final scorers at the Mexico City Grand Prix were Liam Lawson (P7), Gabriel Bortoleto (P8), Hadjar (P9) and Hirakawa (P10).

title: Antonelli’s dad reflects on son’s ‘important’ title triumph
excerpt:
Kimi Antonelli’s father has praised his son for his maiden World Championship victory at the Mexico City Grand Prix, reflecting on their “special” relationship and “very difficult” journey to success.

After the 20-year-old clinched third place behind race winner Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton, giving him enough of a points advantage in the standings to win the title, he embraced his family in an emotional celebration.

It was no surprise that he ran to them after getting out of the car, especially as Marco Antonelli has supported the Italian throughout his motorsport career and was spotted in the Mercedes garage at times this season.

Summarising his reaction to what will be an unforgettable day for the family, he told Sky Sports F1: “Step by step he makes himself stronger and stronger and stronger, and this is the result.

“I'm very lucky because the relationship with my son and with my daughter is special, and this is the best thing in the world that I can have.

“Of course Kimi is young and needs the shoulder in the difficult and also in happy moments, [to] share the situation with somebody that he believes is on his side. I did nothing special, I did only the job that I think that each father [does] with his son and his family, and so we are here. I'm very proud about it.”

Having started the race from P4 on the grid, Antonelli later snatched third from Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc and was able to celebrate his groundbreaking achievement on the podium as he became Italy’s first World Champion in 73 years.

But his triumph also meant a lot on a personal level, as Antonelli senior explained to F1 TV: “I feel good because you can imagine that, when you achieve one result like this, it's an important result and I'm very happy. I said to him, I don't know if you know, you are the champion. I cried!

“It's been step by step during his career that, on some occasion, I realised that he was good. But [you] never can say that he might achieve this result, because it's not possible to say. Never you can [be sure] to be World Champion one day.

“The position that Kimi had last year was very difficult, because when you jump in the car of a seven-time World Champion, it's very difficult to keep up the performance and not feel the pressure.

“I'm very happy that after the bad period he had the capacity to restart and take the experience for improving himself, and I think that this is the result.

“For me the celebration is here on track – around the fans, around you, around the cars. This is my life.”

title: Leclerc concedes he 'deserved penalty' over Hamilton clash
excerpt:
Charles Leclerc has admitted the penalty he recieved for passing team mate Lewis Hamilton off track during an opening lap battle for the Mexico City Grand Prix lead was "deserved".

The Ferrari pair tangled in Turn 4 after the race start as both cars went wide while jostling for position, with the Monegasque driver jumping ahead by going over the grass.

Instead of handing back the position, Leclerc opted to keep going though his decision was influenced by the presence of eventual race winner Max Verstappen who had slotted into second amid the Ferrari duo's battle.

Hamilton was left frustrated with the move, despite Leclerc being hit with a five-second penalty, as he claimed over the radio that running in clean air negated the punishment. The seven-time World Champion eventually went on to reclaim positions on the race restart, and took second while Leclerc was left to settle for fourth on the road.

"The penalty was deserved in a way," said Leclerc, reflecting on the incident after the race.

"The thing is that it was a bit confusing because we both didn’t make Turn 4. Then I stayed ahead, and then Max got past Lewis. So yeah, then I asked what should I do? And I kept the position and took a deserved penalty.”

While a standard penalty for such an incident is often a 10-second penalty, the stewards decided the mitigating factors were sufficient enough to reduce the size of the penalty awarded. “The baseline penalty guideline is 10 seconds, however in mitigation is the fact that car 44 (Hamilton) was also off track on the inside of car 16 (Leclerc) and this occurred early in the first lap," read the decision document explaining the call.

With Hamilton continuing to voice his disgruntlement over the radio, Leclerc insisted he would speak to his team mate and the rest of the team about what happened.

“I think we both didn’t make the corner," he continued. "I don’t know if Lewis’ point was for me to get P3. But at least having a Red Bull in second, I felt it was worth it to kind of keep the position and see what happens. That’s what I did."

The Monegasque was also adamant that the incident was part of racing, adding: “I mean, I could also be unhappy with how much he pushed me off the track out of Turn 1. But I think it’s racing. When you are fighting for a win, it’s the way it should be.”

With Ferrari's intra-team talks now pending between both sides of the garage, the squad head to Brazil next weekend 124 points ahead of Red Bull in the Constructors' Championship in the fight for second place.

title: Piastri receives post-race penalty at Mexico City GP
excerpt:
Oscar Piastri has lost his P7 finish in the Mexico City Grand Prix after receiving a 10-second time penalty for causing a collision with Racing Bulls driver Arvid Lindblad.

The McLaren racer had recovered well from his surprise Q2 exit that left him in the P12 grid slot at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez, improving to the top 10 early on before progressing to seventh through the pit stops.

However, Lindblad found a way past on the Safety Car restart and demoted Piastri to P8, which the Aussie quickly sought to reverse. Coming around the outside at Turn 1, he held on until his front tyre made contact with Lindblad's left rear, sending the latter skidding into the barriers.

As a result, Piastri was handed a time penalty and has dropped to P15 in the classification, promoting Audi's Gabriel Bortoleto into the points.

"The Stewards heard from the driver of Car 81 (Piastri), the driver of Car 41 (Lindblad), team representatives and reviewed positioning/marshalling system data, video and in-car video evidence," read the stewards’ decision document.

"On the approach to turn 1 the driver of Car 81 attempted an overtake on the outside of Car 41. Car 81 was never fully alongside Car 41 so was not able to claim the right to the corner. Through turn 1, the driver of Car 41 defended his position by releasing the brakes however does not force Car 81 off the track, allowing racing room on the outside – which he is not required to do.

"The Stewards determined that the collision could have been avoided if the driver of Car 81 had moved further to the left after turn 1, even if this involved leaving the track prior to turn 2."

Piastri therefore leaves Mexico City with zero points, marking his fourth non-scoring round of the season after Australia, Hungary and Azerbaijan.

title: Verstappen on the move that earned him ‘fantastic’ Mexico win
excerpt:
Max Verstappen believes that Ferrari “made it a little bit difficult for themselves” as their intra-team battle gave him a perfect chance to gain a position and chase down victory at the Mexico City Grand Prix, marking his third win of the season.

An incident with Racing Bulls’ Liam Lawson and a badly-timed lock-up in Qualifying meant that Verstappen started the race from fifth on the grid, but a great start propelled him to P3 on the opening lap.

From there, he capitalised on an off-track moment for Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc up ahead to move into second place, with the Monegasque later handed a five-second time penalty for leaving the circuit and gaining a lasting advantage.

Red Bull’s strategy then saw them call Verstappen into the pits at the same time as Leclerc, allowing him to overtake his penalised rival and secure the race lead, which he maintained all the way to the chequered flag.

“We gave it everything,” he said after pipping Hamilton by just 0.799s. “The first start was good – that, of course, already made my race.

“I think the team also really gave me the right strategy to pit together with Charles and then overtake him in the pit stop because of the penalty. Then it was just fighting to the end, because I think Ferrari today were really fast.

“I do think they made it a little bit difficult for themselves, fighting each other, and that’s why I could capitalise on that.

“I mean, I’ll take it, right? I always try to go for every opportunity and today I saw the opportunity.

“It was a cool fight until the end – Lewis was flat-out in my gearbox so I couldn’t afford to make a mistake.”

Verstappen was under pressure from Hamilton on both restarts, respectively the result of Valtteri Bottas’ suspension failure and a crash for Arvid Lindblad after the Racing Bulls driver and McLaren’s Oscar Piastri made contact.

Hamilton’s failure to find a way past has had an impact on the contest for P2 in the Drivers’ Championship, with Verstappen now two points ahead of Hamilton after Kimi Antonelli sealed his maiden title.

Asked what he can take from the weekend as a whole, Verstappen replied: “It’s always so difficult around here, this track, to get everything right. It’s so slippery as well, and never easy to feel super confident with the car.

“We come out of it with a win, so that’s fantastic. We just keep learning from our weaknesses, our strengths, and apply that also for next year.”

title: Liam Lawson 'takes responsibility' for critical error after Racing Bulls fightback
excerpt:
Liam Lawson has taken responsibility for the qualifying error which led to his disqualification from Mexico City GP qualifying after "a lot was going through my head."

Lawson had qualified eighth on the road in Mexico, but was then shuffled back one place for his penalty due to the FP2 incident with Max Verstappen.

However, just after completing his Q2 lap, he did not lift off the throttle in time, meaning his power unit exceeded the maximum power rampdown limit - leading to a straightforward technical disqualification.

From the pit-lane after engine part changes, Lawson rallied back to ninth place on the road to originally score two points for Racing Bulls - as he continues to await a decision on whether he will keep his seat for 2027.

However, a 10-second time penalty for Oscar Piastri demoted the Australian out of the points and the New Zealander up to eighth, before Franco Colapinto received a 10-second penalty for ignoring blue flags, meaning Lawson was classified seventh - from the pit-lane - and took his points tally for the year to 83 with a third six-point haul in the last four races.

"I think we should have got one more [place] at the end; there was a gap there, and I didn't go for it, which I should have," Lawson told media, including RacingNews365 of his final lap and an attempted move on Colapinto, who finished 0.695s ahead before his penalty.

"But ultimately, it was a good race to come from where we started in the pit lane, and the first part of the race just didn't go our way; we didn't box under the VSC, and then we boxed the lap before the safety car.

"So it was a tough race up until the restart, and then we had a good restart, a good lap one, but it is frustrating as on the first lap [after the restart], I had my dash go to VSC for a split second, so I backed off.

"Then it went away, so I lost one or two spots, which is just frustrating when you're in a race to have your dash do that, but it is a tough race, but a good result from where we started.

Then pushed on his qualifying error which ultimately led to his disqualification from the session, Lawson took responsibility after a "long weekend", including the Max Verstappen incident in FP2.

"It has been a long weekend, honestly," he said.

"There was a lot going through my head [on Saturday], and I was a split-second too late lifting off, and obviously it is very punishing.

"So I take responsibility on that, and it meant we started from the pit-lane, and it probably cost us maybe a place on track."

[Article continues below]

Lawson vs Gasly

Turning to his late duel with Gasly, Lawson explained that his rival was not "generous" in ceding the position back with the incident briefly under investigation.

"It surprised me, he just locked up and went off into Turn 1," Lawson said.

"Then he rejoined, so I said he had to give the place back. We touched wheel and he wasn't very generous giving the place back, but I got it back."

title: Alpine handed double-hammer blow as major punishments confirmed
excerpt:
Alpine has been handed a double-hammer blow following the Mexico City Grand Prix, with both Pierre Gasly and Franco Colapinto receiving heavy post-race punishments.

Colapinto and Gasly had finished in seventh and ninth, scoring the French outfit a strong eight points in its late pursuit of Racing Bulls in the fight for fifth in the constructors' standings.

However, it was soon announced after the race that both drivers had to visit the stewards for alleged yellow flag infringement, of which Gasly an Colapinto have been punished.

Gasly has received a time converted stop-and-go penalty and two penalty points, demoting him from ninth to last (P17), while Colapinto has received a 10-second time penalty and one penalty point which drops him outside the points to 15th.

Remarkably, it promotes rookie Ryo Hirakawa into 10th, meaning a point finish on his debut for Haas. It also promotes Liam Lawson into seventh.

For Gasly's significant punishment, the stewards' report read: "The Stewards heard from the driver of Car 10 (Pierre Gasly), team representative and reviewed positioning/marshalling system data, video, timing, telemetry and in-car video evidence.

"The driver and team representative claimed that the driver had made a significant reduction in speed in the double yellow flag sector however a detailed examination of the telemetry and that of other cars passing through that sector, led the Stewards to conclude that the small reduction noted was not sufficient to satisfy the requirements of the regulations."

Colapinto's was not as severe as the Frenchman's, with the stewards' report reading for the Argentinian's breach: "The Stewards heard from the driver of Car 43 (Franco Colapinto), team representative and reviewed positioning/marshalling system data, video, timing, telemetry, team radio and in-car video evidence.

"The driver and team presented telemetry and photographic evidence claiming it demonstrated that the driver had complied with the regulations which state that the driver must reduce speed and be prepared to change direction. A detailed examination of the telemetry and on board camera failed to satisfy the Stewards that the driver had sufficiently reduced speed through that single yellow sector.

"In relation to the previous double yellow flag sector the Stewards determined that there was sufficient doubt that the driver had sufficient warning in order to comply with the requirements, so did not determine that there was any breach in relation to that sector."

title: George Russell facing punishment on day of Mercedes celebration
excerpt:
George Russell has been summoned by F1 stewards following Kimi Antonelli being crowned world champion in the Mexico City Grand Prix.

With third place, Antonelli became the 36th F1 world champion, and the youngest ever, with Russell's season finally ending in defeat as he took sixth place - having started in second place.

title: Oscar Piastri stripped of Mexico points after huge F1 stewards penalty
excerpt:
Oscar Piastri has been stripped of his points haul in the Mexico City Grand Prix after a severe 10-second post-race penalty.

The Australian had crossed the line in seventh place, but was placed under investigation for a late collision with the Racing Bulls machine of Arvid Lindblad at Turn 1 and 2.

Piastri attempted to move around the outside of Turn 1 to grab the inside of Turn 2, but collected the left-rear of Lindblad's car, destroying it and sending him in the barriers, with the safety car being deployed - with the McLaren suffering severe sidepod and bargeboard damage.

Ultimately, Piastri crossed the line 19.475s behind winner Max Verstappen, but was handed a 10-second penalty by the stewards - dropping him from seventh to 15th in the results.

Franco Colapinto, Liam Lawson, and Pierre Gasly all move up one place, with Gabriel Bortoleto moving into the points in P10.

However, Colapinto and Gasly are being investigated for an alleged yellow flag infringement, and could yet lose their points.

In their verdict, the stewards found that Piastri was "never fully alongside" Lindblad, "so was not able to claim the right to the corner."

It was found that Piastri "could have avoided the collision if he had moved further to the left after Turn 1, even if this involved leaving the track prior to Turn 2."

title: Furious Ferrari boss lays into Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc for 'lack of respect'
excerpt:
A furious Fred Vasseur has accused Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc of showing a "lack of respect" to Ferrari following their Mexico City GP clash.

Hamilton started on pole in Mexico and was primed to tow Leclerc from third down to Turn 1, with the latter moving to the outside of the turn to move up the inside of Turn 2, with Hamilton ahead on the run to Turn 4.

There, Leclerc attempted to swing around the outside, with both he and Hamilton running off the track, as Leclerc got ahead by cutting the track, with Ferrari's misery then compounded by Max Verstappen getting ahead of Hamilton.

Leclerc was subsequently handed a five-second time penalty by the stewards for gaining a lasting advantage, with Hamilton remarking over the radio that the stewards had handed Leclerc a win by only giving him five seconds of penalty, as he still enjoyed clean air.

Verstappen got ahead through the pit-stops as Leclerc served his penalty, with the Red Bull fending off Hamilton's late pursuit through a second standing restart and safety car period to snatch the win - with Red Bull now holding three wins in 2026 to Ferrari's two.

Hamilton was second and Leclerc fourth - but post-race, a furious Vasseur tore into his drivers.

"I'm struggling to swallow it because, honestly, I think it's a lack of respect, a lack of respect for the brand, a lack of respect for all the people working here and for the efforts we're putting in," Vasseur told Canal+.

"We've taken a real step forward in terms of performance, and I think throwing away a win like that is tough."

When then asked if he was directly calling out Leclerc, Vasseur denied the Monegasque was the target of his frustrations and wanted to speak with both drivers.

"No, no, I didn't target anyone; I want to talk with them," he said.

"Lewis was running very wide too, but look, I think we also need to keep in mind that we represent a brand, we represent sponsors, we've got 2,000 people working behind us who aren't just racing for the sake of racing; they're racing for the whole team."

title: Kimi Antonelli title history hailed as 'only the beginning' of F1 legacy
excerpt:
Stefano Domenicali has declared that Kimi Antonelli's world championship marks the start of an "extraordinary legacy" after the Mercedes driver became Formula 1's youngest champion.

Antonelli sealed the 2026 drivers' title by finishing third in the Mexico City Grand Prix. The 20-year-old also becomes the first Italian to win the championship since Alberto Ascari in 1953, ending a 73-year wait for the country.

The Mercedes driver's rise has been rapid. Signed to the Brackley-based squad's junior programme back in 2019, Antonelli was fast-tracked straight into Formula 2 for 2024, skipping Formula 3 entirely, before stepping into a Mercedes race seat in 2025.

F1 CEO Domenicali framed Antonelli's achievement as historic on multiple fronts.

"Today, Kimi Antonelli has made history," said Domenicali. "Becoming the youngest F1 world champion is an extraordinary achievement, earned through exceptional talent, courage and determination."

"It fills me with immense pride to see Kimi become the first Italian Formula 1 world champion since Alberto Ascari in 1953.

"For 73 years, our country has waited for this moment, and today an entire nation will celebrate one of its own reaching the very pinnacle of our sport."

[Article continues below]

Antonelli 'inspiring a generation'

Domenicali went on to tie Antonelli's achievement to its wider impact beyond the result itself.

"Greatness is measured not only by records, but by the generations it inspires," he added.

"Kimi has captured the imagination of millions of fans around the world and shown young people everywhere that there are no limits to what can be achieved through dedication, belief and hard work.

"Across the world, young boys and girls watching today will see in Kimi someone who proves that the biggest dreams can become reality."

The F1 boss then delivered the line that placed Antonelli's triumph in a longer context.

"Today, his name joins the legends of our sport," he said. "A new chapter in F1 history has been written, and I firmly believe this is only the beginning of an extraordinary legacy.

"Congratulations to Kimi, Mercedes and his family on this incredible achievement. The entire F1 community is proud to celebrate this special moment with them."

title: Lewis Hamilton demands 'serious talks' after Charles Leclerc incident fury
excerpt:
Lewis Hamilton has demanded "serious talks" with Ferrari after being left furious by an opening-lap incident with team-mate Charles Leclerc.

Hamilton started the Mexico City Grand Prix from pole position but fell to third by the exit of Turn 5. Leclerc gained a position on the Briton after going across the grass following a moment while the pair were side-by-side, resulting in a five-second time penalty.

The incident with Leclerc also allowed Max Verstappen to pass Hamilton, with the Dutchman going on to claim the race win after moving ahead of the Monegasque while he served his penalty.

Hamilton was furious with the penalty but did at least recover to finish second. He maximised a race restart following a red flag and overtook Leclerc, although he had no answer to Verstappen.

Despite the 41-year-old's annoyance, his immediate thoughts after the race were on Kimi Antonelli, who finished third and was crowned 2026 F1 world champion.

"Firstly, look at this crowd. We have to acknowledge them," said Hamilton.

"A huge congratulations to Kimi and the Mercedes team. It’s great to see them all up here celebrating their success.

"Youngest world champion ever, it’s pretty phenomenal, and I’m so grateful to be in the race to witness it.

"Tough day. I think we had the pace to win today, but it wasn't meant to be. We'll take it offline and see what we can do in the background."

Lewis Hamilton demands Ferrari answers after latest clash

While Hamilton was delighted for his Mercedes replacement, his words on the incident with Leclerc were clear: he was furious.

Hamilton was perplexed as to why it was only a five-second time penalty and not a 10-second punishment, and declared that the clash had cost him the win.

Asked for his thoughts on Leclerc's penalty, Hamilton responded: "In the drivers’ briefing, we discussed as soon as you go off in Turn 1, you have to give the position back. Last year I got a 10-second penalty for that same move that he did.

"But ultimately, it was that that lost us the win today. I think we have to have some serious talks behind the scenes, for sure.

"But the good thing is the team are working really hard. We’ve really improved our car. It’s great to be here, and we were on the old engine this weekend as well.

"Good results, good points. Shame we didn’t get a win, but some you win, some you lose."

title: Max Verstappen made to 'sweat' by Lewis Hamilton in fierce Mexico pursuit
excerpt:
Max Verstappen has described how he was "made to sweat" by Lewis Hamilton during their fierce late chase for Mexico City Grand Prix victory.

Starting fifth after his one place grid penalty, Verstappen was up to second place on the opening lap after passing Lewis Hamilton following his Turn 4 incident with team-mate Charles Leclerc.

Verstappen then held station behind Leclerc until the pair pitted on the same lap, with Verstappen overtaking Leclerc as he served a five-second time penalty for the Hamilton incident.

Thereafter, Verstappen led after Hamilton had pitted, with the Red Bull holding P1 throughout the red flag for Valterri Bottas's crash.

Verstappen then held onto the lead through Turns 1/2/3 against Hamilton after the standing restart, and comfortably held the Ferrari at arm's length through a late safety car for Arvid Lindblad's crash with Oscar Piastri.

It was enough to give Verstappen his third win of the season, and 74th overall, and his sixth in Mexico after 2017, 2018, 2021, 2022, and 2023.

"It was very hectic out there, but I think the first start made the race for me," said Verstappen.

"I had a very good first lap, and then we had a bit of a different strategy, but we hung in there and made the right calls at the right time.

"Of course, the penalty of Charles put us in the lead, and then you could see they were always staying with me, so it was tough.

"I was sweating at the end to try and keep Lewis behind.

"It's such a long run to Turn 1 and then to pick your breaking point there with a big bump in the middle of the track, I had to be quite careful - and then it is always a tradition in Turn 1 that two cars are fighting for the lead."

Turning to Kimi Antonelli's title glory with his third-place finish, Verstappen spoke of the 36thdriver to be champion.

"It is incredible. What a season he's had and to do that at such an age, I think, is really impressive.

"It's amazing to see the whole team celebrating with him, and his family is here as well, so I'm sure this is an emotional day, and I am very proud of him."

title: Is this the most fitting podium in Formula 1 as history made in Mexico?
excerpt:
It was a remarkable sight as two of the most decorated drivers in Formula 1 celebrated on the podium with the youngest champion in the sport's history at the end of the Mexico City Grand Prix.

Kimi Antonelli might not have won the race at the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez, but what he achieved was comfortably enough to set a new F1 record that may never be beaten.

The 20-year-old Italian was third at the chequered flag at the end of 71 laps, joining two of F1's greats on the rostrum.

Four-time F1 champion Max Verstappen took the chequered flag from fifth on the grid in his Red Bull, whilst polesitter Lewis Hamilton was forced to settle for second after a contentious opening lap with Ferrari's Charles Leclerc.

But standing on the podium with 12 titles now between them, it was a remarkable sight.

Perhaps the most fitting podium in Formula 1 at the end of a grand prix as two generational greats stood shoulder to shoulder with a young driver joining them with such an accolade.
